cases.customer_question: How should Bluetooth qualification testing be scheduled when laboratory availability is constrained by calibration or resource limitations?
cases.actual_issue: Testing needed to be completed before a period when the laboratory would be unavailable due to test-system calibration, requiring early sample delivery, resource reservation, and engineering assignment.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Qualification schedules can be affected by laboratory maintenance, calibration, or limited engineering resources. When availability is restricted, testing must be scheduled in advance and resources reserved before samples arrive. Early coordination reduces the risk of project delays.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant informed stakeholders that testing could not be performed during the upcoming unavailable period and arranged for sample arrival before that window. RF and RF-PHY testing dates were scheduled in advance, and laboratory and engineer assignments were requested before formal order completion so execution could proceed without interruption.
cases.decision_logic: When qualification resources are constrained, schedule preservation becomes a qualification-planning requirement. Samples, engineers, laboratories, and administrative processing should be coordinated in parallel to ensure testing occurs during the available window.
cases.final_recommendation: Identify laboratory availability constraints early, secure sample-delivery dates, reserve testing resources, and assign engineers before the execution window begins.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Testing may be postponed until the next available laboratory window, delaying qualification execution and extending the overall project timeline.
